chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

For one hand there is half of the diyah, and for both hands together there is the full diyah; and regarding the two legs likewise. And for the male organ, if the glans is cut off, there is the full diyah, and for what is beyond that as well. And for the nose, if the soft protruding part is cut off, there is the full diyah. And for the two lips there is the full diyah, and for the two eyes there is the full diyah, and for one of them there is half of the diyah.

key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation legally due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.اَلشَّفَتَيْنِ: the two lips, for which the full diyah is due
key_terms.اَلْحَشَفَةُ: the glans of the male organ, whose severance entails the full diyah
key_terms.اَلْعَيْنَيْنِ: the two eyes, for which the full diyah is due
key_terms.اَلْمَارِنُ: the soft projecting part of the nose, whose severance entails the full diyah
key_terms.اَلْيَدَيْنِ: the two hands together, for which the full diyah is due
key_terms.اَلْيَدِ: the hand, for which half of the diyah is assigned when one is lost

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due in Shia fiqh for injury to organs such as the hand, eye, nose, lips, legs, and male organ?
ai.summary: This hadith states fixed legal rulings for diyah concerning the loss or severance of specific bodily organs. It specifies when a full diyah is due and when half of the diyah applies, forming part of the jurisprudence of bodily injury and compensation.
